name: GRAIL twin probes Ebb and Flow

location.name: Unnamed mountain in the Moon's northern highlands

headline: Twin probes mapped the Moon's gravity, then flew into a mountain on purpose
story: Ebb and Flow left Cape Canaveral together on 10 September 2011 on a single Delta II and took a slow, three-and-a-half-month route to the Moon. One entered lunar orbit on 31 December 2011, the other about a day later. Then they lined up, one behind the other, about 50 kilometers above the surface.

A radio link measured the changing distance between them. Where the Moon's gravity pulled a little harder, the gap shifted. From those tiny shifts, GRAIL built the highest-resolution gravity map of any world at the time and pinpointed mascons, dense masses hidden beneath the surface where no camera can see. Each probe also carried MoonKAM cameras for middle school students, an education project run with Sally Ride Science.

On 17 December 2012, with their mapping done, both probes were steered into a mountain in the Moon's far north at roughly 1.7 kilometers per second. They came down about two kilometers apart on its slope.
